**Source 1:**  
Publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)  
Title: Myths and Facts about COVID-19 Vaccines  
Publish Date: February 16, 2023  
Details: For claim c1, the CDC states that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and are not administered to track individuals' movements [1]. The agency explains that vaccines work strictly to stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies and do not contain tracking components [1].

**Source 2:**  
Publisher: Kementerian Komunikasi dan Informatika RI (Kominfo) via Pemprov DKI Jakarta (Jalahoaks)  
Title: [HOAKS] - Vaksin COVID-19 Memiliki Chip Yang Dapat Melacak Keberadaan Orang  
Publish Date: January 21, 2021  
Details: For claim c1, official spokespersons clarified that claims stating COVID-19 vaccines contain a microchip to track individuals are false (hoaks) [2]. The authorities explained that barcodes and tracking elements belong strictly to packaging and distribution logistics (such as tracking vaccine vials) and do not enter or remain in vaccinated recipients [2].

**Source 3:**  
Publisher: AFP Fact Check  
Title: Covid-19 vaccines do not contain tracking devices  
Publish Date: July 2, 2021  
Details: For claim c1, infectious disease specialists and health regulators in the United States and Canada confirmed that authorized COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips or tracking devices [3]. The report notes that false claims circulating on social media regarding microchip detection in vaccine recipients stem from fabricated or misrepresented videos [3].

**Source 4:**  
Publisher: FactCheck.org  
Title: COVID-19 Vaccines Don’t Have Microchips  
Publish Date: December 15, 2020  
Details: For claim c1, the fact-check clarifies that viral assertions about microchip tracking originated from misleading interpretations of optional RFID tags used on external syringe packaging [4]. Those tags serve strictly as serial barcodes for vaccine vial logistics and expiration management, containing no patient information and possessing no ability to be injected or track human movement [4].

**Source 5:**  
Publisher: Mayo Clinic Health System  
Title: COVID-19 vaccine myths debunked  
Publish Date: October 11, 2021  
Details: For claim c1, medical directors confirmed there are no microchips in COVID-19 vaccines, nor any mechanism to track or gather personal information through an injection [5]. The article traces the conspiracy theory back to distorted remarks regarding digital records, emphasizing that no tracking microchip technology is part of the vaccine formulation [5].
